contractSeal.guarantees: This file is sealed with Verikora's key (Ed25519, held by Krizaka): it attests that this content, these parties and these dates existed in this form at the time of sealing and have not been changed since.
contractSeal.notGuaranteed: It does not verify anyone's identity, the age of anyone, the validity of the contract in law or the partner's statements: Verikora checks documents, it does not decide. Informative, not legal advice.
contractSeal.verify: To check a copy, take its SHA-256 and open {url} followed by that value: the answer says whether Verikora sealed it and when, and shows no personal information.

ownerReport.title: Verification report
ownerReport.lead: What was examined on an applicant's file, for the building owner. Hashes only: no document, no name, no quoted passage.
ownerReport.notice: Informative verification, not legal advice. A person decides; this report decides nothing and ranks no one.
ownerReport.noSignals: No signal was observed on this document.
ownerReport.noFindings: No rule was checked on this document.
ownerReport.reviewStatus: Ruleset review status: {status}. It is to be read by a lawyer before it is relied upon.
ownerReport.limits: What this report does not show: the documents themselves, the person's name or contact, any grade or ranking. The signals are observations about a file, never a judgement of a person.
ownerReport.guarantees: This PDF is signed with Verikora's key (Ed25519, held by Krizaka). The signature covers every item of this report (documents, signals, rules checked, runs, versions), the link's expiry and the full text of the pages. If a single character changes, verification fails.
ownerReport.notGuaranteed: It does not prove that the signals or findings are right, nor who holds the file: it shows no name, contact, file name or quoted passage. Informative, not legal advice; a person decides.
ownerReport.signatureNote: The attestation (payload, text fingerprint and signature) is embedded in the PDF. Any change to the text of the earlier pages makes verification fail.
ownerReport.footer: Verikora, a Krizaka product — analysis by Sovkora.
ownerReport.languageNote: The rules are written in French; the English names come with the ruleset. Article references are given as cited.

sectionG.previous-blank: Section G of the lease is blank: the lowest rent paid in the twelve months before the lease is not stated (C.c.Q., art. 1896).
sectionG.previous-altered: Section G of the lease looks altered: check the figure against the landlord's notice (C.c.Q., art. 1896).
sectionG.over-rate: The new rent is {excess} a month above the highest rent the TAL's {year} rate gives from the stated previous rent ({max}). Source: {source}.
sectionG.within-rate: The new rent is within the highest rent the TAL's {year} rate gives from the stated previous rent ({max}). Source: {source}.
sectionG.not-above-previous: The new rent is not above the previous rent stated in Section G.
sectionG.no-rate: No claim: the TAL's rate for this year is not entered, or the figures are not usable, so the increase is not compared.
sectionG.recourse: Recourse: the tenant may ask the Tribunal administratif du logement to fix the rent (C.c.Q., art. 1950).
sectionG.disclaimer: Information about the figures and dates of the lease, not legal advice and no judgement on the landlord. Check the article and the TAL's page, or ask the TAL: it tells you the form and any fee, and how days and months are counted. Verikora files nothing.

paymentClauses.advance-over-one-month: The lease asks for more than one month of rent in advance. A landlord may require only the first term, within one month (C.c.Q., art. 1904).
paymentClauses.deposit: The lease asks for a sum besides the rent (deposit, key money or guarantee). A landlord may not require one (C.c.Q., art. 1904).
paymentClauses.postdated-cheques: The lease requires postdated cheques. A landlord may not require them (C.c.Q., art. 1904).
paymentClauses.ok: The payment terms read in the lease stay within what art. 1904 allows (C.c.Q., art. 1904).
paymentClauses.disclaimer: Information about the terms of the lease, not legal advice and no judgement on the landlord. Check the article, or ask the TAL.

sectionGDeadline.ten-days: The landlord gave the notice: the request to the TAL is made within 10 days of the day the lease was concluded.
sectionGDeadline.two-months-from-start: No notice was given: the request to the TAL is made within two months of the start of the lease.
sectionGDeadline.two-months-from-knowledge: The notice held a false statement: the request to the TAL is made within two months of learning of it.
sectionGDeadline.open: By these dates, the last day to ask is {lastDay} ({days} days left). Source: {source}.
sectionGDeadline.last-day: By these dates, today ({lastDay}) is the last day to ask. Source: {source}.
sectionGDeadline.closed: By these dates, the last day to ask was {lastDay}. Source: {source}.
sectionGDeadline.no-claim: No claim: a date is missing or unreadable, so no deadline is given.

sectionGRequest.title: Facts to take to the TAL:
sectionGRequest.rentPrevious: Lowest rent in the twelve months before, as written in Section G: {cents}.
sectionGRequest.previousBlank: Section G of the lease does not state the previous rent.
sectionGRequest.previousAltered: Section G of the lease looks crossed out or altered.
sectionGRequest.rentMax: Highest rent the TAL's {year} rate gives from that previous rent: {cents}.
sectionGRequest.deadline: By the dates given, the last day to ask the TAL to fix the rent is {lastDay}.

renewalNotice.title: Notice of renewal with a rent increase
renewalNotice.refusal: You have one month from receiving this notice to refuse the increase; the landlord may then ask the Tribunal administratif du logement to set the rent.
renewalNotice.disclaimer: Prepared with Verikora as information, not legal advice. The landlord checks it, signs it and sends it themselves: Verikora sends nothing on anyone's behalf.
